What LSOV, ARP and ATRP mean

LSOV — Local Share of Voice. The share of your grid points where you rank in the top 3. One number for how much of the neighbourhood actually sees the business near the top of the map. It’s the figure a client follows month to month.

ARP — Average Rank where Present. Your average position across only the points where you were found in the top 20. It tells you how high you rank where you rank at all.

ATRP — Average Total Rank Position. The same average, but every point where you’re missing counts as 21. It turns “not in the top 20” into a number that can improve — so the invisible parts of the map are measured, not ignored.

A fourth figure is simply what the scan costs: one credit per grid point searched — 81 at 9 × 9, 441 at 21 × 21. Together they turn a grid of pins into an answer: how wide a business wins, how high it ranks, and what it costs to watch.

Questions, answered

What is LSOV in local SEO?

LSOV — Local Share of Voice — is the share of a scan’s grid points where the business ranks in the top 3. It’s one number for how much of the neighbourhood sees it near the top of the map, and the figure a client follows month to month.

What is ARP?

ARP — Average Rank where Present — is your average position across only the points where you appear in the top 20. It tells you how high you rank where you rank at all.

What is ATRP?

ATRP — Average Total Rank Position — is the same average, but every point where you’re missing counts as 21. It turns “not in the top 20” into a number that can improve, so the invisible parts of the map are measured, not ignored.

Which number should I report to a client?

LSOV is the headline — one percentage for whether the business is winning the map. ARP and ATRP sit beside it when you need the detail of how high and how wide.

How is scan cost calculated?

One credit per grid point searched — 81 at 9 × 9, 441 at 21 × 21 — and credits never expire.
